result.title: Rethinking Post-hoc Debiasing of Large Pretrained Models
result.summary: Large pretrained models such as CLIP are widely used as frozen feature extractors. However, their embeddings inherit spurious correlations from training data, introducing bias into the features. A growing body of research has sought to address this issue through post hoc debiasing, leaving the backbone untouched. We discover that despite differing mechanisms, these methods require the bias feature to be identified and expressed in text. This dependency is not innocuous. In this work, we experimentally demonstrate that this requirement incurs an unforeseen penalty in certain scenarios. For example, on the UrbanCars benchmark, having two co-occurring bias attributes, the recent methods underperform a vanilla classifier on biased frozenbackbone features, and even providing ground-truth bias identities does not close the gap. We show that the pattern that such methods seek is readily observable in the frozen geometry. Specifically, cross-class training pairs placed closest together by the frozen encoder almost always share a spurious attribute, regardless of the bias type, without requiring access to the bias labels. Based on this, we propose a novel approach to identify such pairs and learn a single linear map that transforms the features to perform post-hoc debiasing. The proposed approach achieves competitive performance across all datasets without access to bias attribute annotations or any LLMs.

AI.brief_summary: 论文指出多种 CLIP 后处理去偏方法依赖以文本形式识别偏见属性，并发现冻结编码器的几何中最近跨类样本常共享虚假属性，据此提出无需偏见标注或 LLM 的样本配对识别与单一线性映射去偏方法。
AI.relevance_reason: 其利用冻结特征几何识别虚假属性、再以线性映射改写表示的做法，可能为 LVR 中抑制视觉捷径、筛选任务相关视觉证据及探查内部表示提供方法线索，但能否迁移到推理状态仍需核查。
